logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, repository code search offers regular-expression matching. Submitting a malformed expression replaces the page with a full Internal Server Error instead of displaying a recoverable search-validation message and allowing the query to be corrected.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Search forwards gitgrep.PerformSearch errors, including invalid regex compilation from git grep, directly to ServerError.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, repository code search offers regular-expression matching. Submitting a malformed expression replaces the page with a full Internal Server Error instead of displaying a recoverable search-validation message and allowing the query to be corrected.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, commit details and branch comparisons summarize the number of changed files. With exactly one changed file, the summary still uses the plural word “files” instead of “file”; the file count itself need not be incorrect.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The stats_desc locale literal uses files unconditionally rather than a singular/plural count-aware variant.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, commit details and branch comparisons summarize the number of changed files. With exactly one changed file, the summary still uses the plural word “files” instead of “file”; the file count itself need not be incorrect.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, branch search and Explore repository-description search can lose a valid substring match when the search text ends in a literal percent sign. Searching the ordinary prefix or another matching substring finds the same saved branch/repository.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Repository name/description searches pass user substrings to builder.Like. Its terminal-percent wildcard handling does not preserve a trailing literal percent as a substring match.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a saved branch containing an allowed percent sign is found by an ordinary substring or full name but disappears for a matching substring ending in percent.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, Add File > Upload File accepts a genuinely empty file, but committing it stores 1,024 zero bytes instead of an empty file. The file page shows 1.0 KiB and View Raw rather than 0 B and The file is empty, and commit or branch comparisons show BIN and Binary file not shown. Downloading can confirm the incorrect stored bytes. Reports of either downstream presentation after a zero-byte upload match without proving a separate rendering defect: the stored bytes actually are binary. Creating an empty file through New File works normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UploadFileToServer allocates a 1024-byte probe and slices it only when n>0; NewUpload writes the entire unsliced zero buffer for an empty file.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, upload File accepts a genuinely empty text file, but committing it stores a nonempty binary file containing a fixed-size buffer instead of zero bytes. Downloading confirms that the content was changed, and the file also acquires the wrong size and loses ordinary text editability.

Upload a genuine zero-byte text file through Add File > Upload File and confirm it is staged as 0 B. Commit it on a new branch, then open its commit diff or compare that branch with its base. The uploaded file is labelled BIN with Binary file not shown, unlike an empty file created through New File. Its file page also shows 1.0 KiB, and downloading reveals 1,024 zero bytes: the binary label describes the corrupted upload correctly.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s repository header combines the Fork action with a separate count link to existing forks. When the current user cannot create a fork and has no existing personal or organization fork, both controls are disabled, preventing read-only access to the forks list even though only creation should be unavailable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The disabled class is applied to the enclosing Fork action group containing both creation and its separate count link, blocking the otherwise readable inventory.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s repository header combines the Fork action with a separate count link to existing forks. When the current user cannot create a fork and has no existing personal or organization fork, both controls are disabled, preventing read-only access to the forks list even though only creation should be unavailable.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, navigate from a repository directory listing to a file, then use browser Back. The address returns to the directory, but the file’s contents and breadcrumb remain on screen instead of restoring the directory listing. Reloading the same address displays the correct directory.
logicalBugs.rootCause: navigateTreeView pushes state only for new navigations; initial history state has no url. popstate loads content only if e.state.url exists, leaving the last file rendered.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s repository Code browser, navigate from a directory listing to a file and then use browser Back. The address points to the directory again, but the file content and breadcrumb remain displayed until reload instead of restoring the directory list.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Add File > New File, enter a filename and inspect the suggested commit-message placeholder. It still contains the literal template token {filename} instead of substituting the entered file name, so the proposed message is unfinished.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The filename editor updates tree_path but does not substitute the {filename} placeholder in the new-file commit message input.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Add File > New File, enter a filename and inspect the suggested commit-message placeholder. It still contains the literal template token {filename} instead of substituting the entered file name, so the proposed message is unfinished.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after syncing a fork with its upstream repository, the fork's commit history renders the upstream merge commit's #3 pull request (a proposed code change) reference as a link under the fork, where that issue (a tracked work item) does not exist. The link opens a 404 instead of the actual upstream pull request.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Commit message issue-reference rendering uses the current repository context, with no upstream origin resolution for a synced upstream merge commit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, synchronize a fork with its upstream repository, then follow a pull request reference in the synchronized upstream merge commit’s message. The reference is resolved within the fork and opens Page Not Found instead of the actual upstream pull request.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, enter a new destination directory but leave the upload queue empty. Submitting is accepted and redirects to that directory even though no files created it, leaving the user on a nonexistent path instead of explaining that nothing was uploaded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UploadFilePost accepts an empty form.Files collection and still builds the redirect to the submitted directory despite no Git tree being created there.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, enter a new destination directory but leave the upload queue empty. Submitting is accepted and redirects to that directory even though no files created it, leaving the user on a nonexistent path instead of explaining that nothing was uploaded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a file’s History page lists commits that changed that file. When exactly one commit exists, the heading reads “1 Commits” instead of the singular “1 Commit.”
logicalBugs.rootCause: The history count renders the fixed commits label rather than count-aware singular wording.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a file’s History page lists commits that changed that file. When exactly one commit exists, the heading reads “1 Commits” instead of the singular “1 Commit.”

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, compare commits can call different branches equal when the selected head is an ancestor of the base. Reversing the comparison shows commits and a file diff, but the ancestor-to-descendant direction shows the equal-branches/empty-comparison message despite different trees.
logicalBugs.rootCause: PrepareCompareDiff sets IsNothingToCompare when headCommitID equals the comparison MergeBase. This uses the empty base-to-head commit range from merge-base semantics as an equality test, although the selected branch trees can differ. Repository comparison and pull-request comparison share this decision.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, reversing the two repository branches makes the read-only Compare commits view claim they are equal, despite the opposite direction showing one commit and a file diff; this persisted after refresh and a repeat reversal.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in repository code search’s Exact mode, a query beginning with one or more literal hyphens can match lines containing the rest of the word without those hyphens. The results therefore omit characters that Exact search should require, rather than matching the complete entered text.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Grep builds the -e pattern using strings.TrimLeft(search,"-") even though -e already safely separates the pattern from options.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, use repository code search in Exact mode with a query starting in one or more literal hyphens. Lines containing only the following word, without those hyphens, are still returned instead of requiring the complete search text.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, RSS feeds opened from a repository branch or file toolbar advertise a channel link without the required /src route segment. Following the channel link opens 404 although the corresponding branch or file page works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ShowFileFeed constructs repo.HTMLURL + RefTypeNameSubURL + TreePath directly instead of the source route prefix.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, from a repository branch toolbar, open its RSS feed and follow the feed’s link back to that branch. The generated address omits the required source-view route and returns Page Not Found, while the actual branch page opens correctly.

In Gitea, from a repository file toolbar, open its RSS feed and follow the feed’s link back to the file. The generated address lacks the required source-view route and returns Page Not Found instead of opening the existing file.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s repository Branches page at tablet width, branch rows retain a layout wider than their visible table. The delete controls extend beyond the table’s outer border instead of staying inside the row with the branch information.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The branches table uses fixed widths and single-line rows containing controls whose intrinsic width exceeds the available tablet columns.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s repository Branches page at tablet width, branch rows retain a layout wider than their visible table. The delete controls extend beyond the table’s outer border instead of staying inside the row with the branch information.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, navigating to a file through the repository file tree updates its content, URL and breadcrumb but leaves the browser tab title on the previous file. Newly loaded Markdown also lacks the heading permalink links present after a full page load.
logicalBugs.rootCause: loadViewContent replaces only repo-view-content.innerHTML. It neither updates document.title nor runs markup anchor initialization on the inserted content.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, open one repository file, then use the file-tree sidebar to navigate to another. The address, breadcrumb and file content update, but the browser tab title keeps the previous file’s name until a full reload.
In Gitea, when a Markdown file is opened by clicking it in the repository file tree, its rendered headings have no anchor (permalink) links. Opening the same file by a full page load shows them.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, repository Code/History can display a commit total from an older or different ref despite showing the current commit/files. Triggers include syncing or uploading commits, renaming/recreating a branch, or viewing a tag after a longer same-named branch; incorrect totals can expose empty history pages until the cached count changes.
logicalBugs.rootCause: GetCommitsCount keys ref caches by RefFullName.ShortName plus a shared ref marker, omitting ref type and tip SHA. Same-named tag/branch collide and ref updates/recreation/rename retain cached history counts.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after the longer same-named branch history has been visited, a tag's Code and History views show the branch's cached commit count even though the tag points to one commit, exposing a nonexistent empty history page.

In Gitea, after Sync fork (or another push made from the web UI), the redirected Code page shows the new head commit and files but the branch's previous 'N Commits' count. History and the next page load show the correct number.

In Gitea, after a branch is renamed or deleted and a new branch is created with the same name from a different commit, the Code page and History show the old branch's 'N Commits' total and pagination while listing the new branch's commits, even after reload.

After committing uploaded files directly to a branch, Gitea redirects to the Code page, which already lists the new commit and file but still shows the previous commit count in the statistics bar. Reloading shows the right count. The count is read from a cache that is refreshed in the background after the push.

In Gitea, create a branch from a history containing multiple commits, then rename that slash-containing branch to a flat name. The Code page’s commit count drops even though the branch’s latest commit and actual history were not changed by the rename.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s repository Code menu offers clone commands and links that open the repository in desktop editors. After selecting Tea CLI, the VS Code, VSCodium and IntelliJ links use the whole “tea clone …” shell command as their repository address instead of a Git URL, so selecting a command format corrupts the editor link targets.
logicalBugs.rootCause: updateClonePanelUi passes the selected tab data-link to every editor URI template; the tea tab data-link is a shell command instead of a clone URL.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea repository’s Code menu, switch the clone format to Tea CLI, then inspect the offered desktop-editor links. VS Code, VSCodium and IntelliJ now receive the full “tea clone …” command as their repository address rather than a usable Git URL.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, source archive downloads can contain a different commit from the branch/tag being viewed when its short name is ambiguous. A branch sharing a name with a tag can download the tag’s tree, and a tag named as another commit’s full SHA can download that spelled commit instead of its actual target.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The release archive URL uses an unqualified tag name, and archive resolution accepts object IDs and other refs, so a SHA-shaped tag name resolves the spelled commit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a branch and a tag share a name but point at different commits, Code → Download ZIP on the branch page links to /archive/<name>.zip and serves the tag's older tree instead of the displayed branch tip, without any warning.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a branch and an older tag share a name, History for a branch file resolves the bare name to the tag. If the tag lacks the file, /commits/branch/<name>/<file> returns a full-page 404; if the tag has it, the page silently lists only the tag's older commits.
logicalBugs.rootCause: FileHistory passes RefFullName.ShortName to FileCommitsCount and history lookup instead of the fully qualified branch ref, so a tag can supply the history or not-found.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a branch and an older tag share a name, History for a branch file resolves the bare name to the tag. If the tag lacks the file, /commits/branch/<name>/<file> returns a full-page 404; if the tag has it, the page silently lists only the tag's older commits.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea can compare versions of a code repository by selecting a branch, which tracks a line of development, or a tag, which labels a version. When a branch and tag have the same name, choosing the tag from the Compare commits selector actually compares the branch instead. The selected name looks right, but the comparison uses the wrong kind of version reference.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The comparison selector encodes the selected tag as its bare name; ParseCompareInfo interprets branch names before tags and loses the selected ref kind.
reproductionPaths: When a branch and a tag share a name, choosing the tag from the Tags tab of the Compare commits selector links to the bare name, and Gitea compares the same-named branch instead of the tag.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s web file editor, Preview Changes ignores a pending rename and can report no changes for a rename-only edit. After a rejected rename to an existing file, correcting the name can instead preview against the attempted existing file rather than the original source.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The diff tab hx-post URL is fixed to original TreePath and hx-params includes only context/content; renames are omitted and rejected-rename state can change which file path the form previews.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s web file editor, Preview Changes sends only the file content to the original path and never the new filename, so a rename-only edit previews as 'There are no changes to show.' even though Commit Changes is enabled and commits a rename.

In Gitea’s file editor, if renaming a file is rejected because the new name already exists (for example README.md), and the name is then corrected, Preview Changes diffs the edit against the rejected name's file instead of the file being edited, and the commit summary suggests updating that other file.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, validation errors show internal field keys instead of visible field names: examples include profile Website, release Tag name/Title, branch rename, protected-tag pattern and repository Default Branch. The input can be correctly rejected while the banner says form.Website, form.TagName or a similar untranslated key.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Validate constructs form.<GoField> labels; Website has no matching translated field label and URL validation appends its internal Url message argument.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, renaming a branch to an invalid name shows an error that names the field with the internal key form.To instead of a readable branch name label.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Branches page, Confirm in Create new branch or Rename Branch closes the dialog when its required name is empty. Nothing is created/renamed and no validation message explains why the command was ignored.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The create/rename modals use approve-style submission without required validation retaining the modal on empty name; the shared branch UI opens them without installing a failed-validation close guard.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Branches page, opening a branch's Create new branch dialog and clicking Confirm with the required Branch Name empty closes the dialog with no message, and no branch is created.

On Gitea’s Branches page, opening Rename Branch and clicking Confirm without entering a new name closes the dialog with no message, and nothing is renamed. The required name field blocks the submit, but the dialog closes before the browser can show why.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a commit opened from a file's History via 'View changes to this file in this commit' shows only that file's diff, but clicking Split/Unified view or a whitespace option drops the file filter and shows every file in the commit again.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Diff layout links reconstruct query parameters from style/whitespace options rather than preserving the current file filter query.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a commit opened from a file's History via 'View changes to this file in this commit' shows only that file's diff, but clicking Split/Unified view or a whitespace option drops the file filter and shows every file in the commit again.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, revert, Cherry-pick and Apply Patch offer Add a Signed-off-by trailer, but commits created with it checked omit that trailer. Other commit content can save successfully, leaving the offered sign-off choice silently ineffective.
logicalBugs.rootCause: These handlers construct ApplyDiffPatchOptions without forwarding form.Signoff, although the shared commit form displays the Sign-off checkbox.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when reverting or cherry-picking a commit from the web UI with 'Add a Signed-off-by trailer' checked, the resulting commit has no Signed-off-by trailer.
In Gitea, committing through Add File > Apply Patch with 'Add a Signed-off-by trailer' checked creates a commit without the Signed-off-by trailer.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, a destination folder containing a .git path segment (such as '.git', 'docs/.git' or '.GIT') is silently ignored: the upload is committed to the repository root instead, with no warning, and can replace a root file with the same name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CleanUploadFileName returns empty for paths containing .git; UploadFilePost uses the sanitized empty path as a valid root destination instead of rejecting the original invalid path.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, a destination folder containing a .git path segment (such as '.git', 'docs/.git' or '.GIT') is silently ignored: the upload is committed to the repository root instead, with no warning, and can replace a root file with the same name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, uploading a file whose name matches an existing directory at the same location (for example a file named 'docs' at the repository root) commits successfully and replaces the directory with the file, deleting every file in it. New File and rename refuse the same name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The upload service stages the target path without rejecting an existing directory; adding a blob at the directory entry replaces the subtree.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, uploading a file whose name matches an existing directory at the same location (for example a file named 'docs' at the repository root) commits successfully and replaces the directory with the file, deleting every file in it. New File and rename refuse the same name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, each uploaded file gets a Copy link button, but the Markdown it copies points to /attachments/<uuid>, which returns 404 Not Found both before and after the files are committed. Repository uploads aren't attachments, so the link can never work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared upload widget builds an attachment URL for a repository-upload UUID, but repository uploads are served through their separate staging path and are not release/issue attachments.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Add File > Upload File, each uploaded file gets a Copy link button, but the Markdown it copies points to /attachments/<uuid>, which returns 404 Not Found both before and after the files are committed. Repository uploads aren't attachments, so the link can never work.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Branches page, a deleted branch (shown with Restore) still has its RSS Feed icon, and clicking it opens a 404 Not Found page. The row's other actions are hidden for deleted branches.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The branches row continues to render its RSS link outside the IsDeleted branch, even though the feed route requires a live Git ref.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Branches page, a deleted branch (shown with Restore) still has its RSS Feed icon, and clicking it opens a 404 Not Found page. The row's other actions are hidden for deleted branches.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a Markdown file is viewed from a folder (or with a file name) containing '#', '%' or '?', its relative images show as broken and its relative links open 404 pages, even though the referenced files exist and open fine directly. The current path is used unescaped when resolving relative links, so the URL is cut or mangled at the special character.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Markdown rendering constructs source/raw context URLs from path text without consistently escaping special URL characters before resolving relative links, so #/?/% alter the resulting URL meaning.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a Markdown file is viewed from a folder (or with a file name) containing '#', '%' or '?', its relative images show as broken and its relative links open 404 pages, even though the referenced files exist and open fine directly. The current path is used unescaped when resolving relative links, so the URL is cut or mangled at the special character.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a file is changed by someone else after its Delete File page was opened, submitting the deletion is correctly refused, but the error shown is the untranslated key 'repo.editor.file_changed_while_deleting' followed by Go formatting diagnostics ('%!(EXTRA string=…)') and a raw compare path, instead of a readable message. Editing a stale file shows a proper message.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The delete handler requests repo.editor.file_changed_while_deleting, which has no matching English locale entry, instead of an existing readable conflict translation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a file is changed by someone else after its Delete File page was opened, submitting the deletion is correctly refused, but the error shown is the untranslated key 'repo.editor.file_changed_while_deleting' followed by Go formatting diagnostics ('%!(EXTRA string=…)') and a raw compare path, instead of a readable message. Editing a stale file shows a proper message.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s web editor's Commit Changes form, choosing Create a new branch and entering the name of the branch being edited isn't rejected as an existing branch. The change is committed straight onto that branch and the user lands on a comparison of the branch with itself saying the branches are equal. Any other existing branch name is correctly refused. The same happens from New File, Upload File, Apply Patch, Delete File, cherry-pick and revert.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The editor passes OldBranch and NewBranch as equal strings; the write service treats equality as direct commit and cannot distinguish the user-selected new-branch intention.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s web editor's Commit Changes form, choosing Create a new branch and entering the name of the branch being edited isn't rejected as an existing branch. The change is committed straight onto that branch and the user lands on a comparison of the branch with itself saying the branches are equal. Any other existing branch name is correctly refused. The same happens from New File, Upload File, Apply Patch, Delete File, cherry-pick and revert.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Upload File page, when committing fails validation (for example the target directory path runs through an existing file, or the new branch name already exists), the page comes back with the error, commit summary and path kept, but the files that were uploaded and staged are gone and must be added again.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The validation re-render does not repopulate the queue with form.Files, so correcting a branch/path error submits without the prior uploads.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Upload File page, when committing fails validation (for example the target directory path runs through an existing file, or the new branch name already exists), the page comes back with the error, commit summary and path kept, but the files that were uploaded and staged are gone and must be added again.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, in Blame view of a Markdown (or other renderable) file, a line's Copy Permalink link opens the file's rendered view, which has no line numbers, so the selected line isn't shown or highlighted. The link is meant to add ?display=source for renderable files, but the blame page never sets the flag that adds it; permalinks copied from the normal source view work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The copy URL adds display=source only when HasSourceRenderedToggle is set; blame does not supply the same toggle state as source view, so Markdown permalink navigation renders prose without source line IDs.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, in Blame view of a Markdown (or other renderable) file, a line's Copy Permalink link opens the file's rendered view, which has no line numbers, so the selected line isn't shown or highlighted. The link is meant to add ?display=source for renderable files, but the blame page never sets the flag that adds it; permalinks copied from the normal source view work.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with a file open in the editor, if the file is renamed or deleted in another tab, clicking Preview Changes shows an 'Error 500' banner and an empty preview. The preview request still uses the original path and treats the missing file as a server error, while committing from the same editor shows a readable message that the file no longer exists.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DiffPreviewPost sends GetTreeEntryByPath not-found errors to HTTPError(500) instead of a stale-file validation response.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with a file open in the editor, if the file is renamed or deleted in another tab, clicking Preview Changes shows an 'Error 500' banner and an empty preview. The preview request still uses the original path and treats the missing file as a server error, while committing from the same editor shows a readable message that the file no longer exists.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, without a code indexer, repository code search uses git grep and only returns the first 50 matching files, but the results page doesn't say the list was truncated: the pager ends at the 50th file as if those were all the matches.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Grep defaults MaxResultLimit to 50 and cancels once reached, but result presentation does not expose a truncation indicator.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, without a code indexer, repository code search uses git grep and only returns the first 50 matching files, but the results page doesn't say the list was truncated: the pager ends at the 50th file as if those were all the matches.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s file editor's path field, Backspace at the very start of the name intentionally pulls the last folder back into the name (the inverse of typing '/'). But the check only looks at where the selection starts, so selecting the whole name and pressing Backspace also triggers it: the selected text isn't deleted, the parent folder is prefixed onto it, and the folder disappears from the path. The same happens in the Upload File directory field.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The keydown branch tests selectionStart==0 but never checks selectionEnd; a selection starting at zero incorrectly triggers moving the last folder into the filename.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s file editor's path field, Backspace at the very start of the name intentionally pulls the last folder back into the name (the inverse of typing '/'). But the check only looks at where the selection starts, so selecting the whole name and pressing Backspace also triggers it: the selected text isn't deleted, the parent folder is prefixed onto it, and the folder disappears from the path. The same happens in the Upload File directory field.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s file editor, after a rename or move is rejected, Cancel points at the attempted destination instead of returning to the original file. If that destination does not exist, Cancel opens a 404; if it is an existing file that caused the name conflict, Cancel opens that other file and its contents. The matching trigger is submitting the change and receiving a validation error, rather than merely typing a new name and cancelling before submission.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The edit submission replaces the template’s current file path with the submitted destination before validating it. When validation fails, both Cancel links are rendered from that rejected destination instead of retaining the original source path. The result is a 404 for an absent destination or navigation to the wrong existing file.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s file editor, if renaming or moving a file is rejected (for example because part of the new path is an existing file), the editor's Cancel link then points at the rejected new path instead of the original file, so clicking Cancel opens a 404. The error page renders with the attempted path as the current file path.

Create two different files in a repository, open the first in Edit File and change its path to the second file’s existing path. Submit the commit and wait for the already-exists validation error. Click either Cancel link: it opens the second file with its own contents rather than returning to the first file. Cancelling before submitting the rename returns to the original file correctly.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Apply Patch page, choosing 'Create a new branch' with the name of a branch that already exists correctly shows 'Branch "<name>" already exists in this repository.', but the rest of the page is a 500 Internal Server Error (a template render failure) instead of the Apply Patch form, so the patch and commit message are lost. The handler renders the file editor's template for this error instead of the patch template.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The branch-exists error path renders tplEditFile rather than tplPatchFile, without the file-editor template data required by that unrelated page.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Apply Patch page, choosing 'Create a new branch' with the name of a branch that already exists correctly shows 'Branch "<name>" already exists in this repository.', but the rest of the page is a 500 Internal Server Error (a template render failure) instead of the Apply Patch form, so the patch and commit message are lost. The handler renders the file editor's template for this error instead of the patch template.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s file editor (also Delete and Upload), after typing an invalid name under 'Create a new branch for this commit' and then switching to 'Commit directly to the branch', the hidden new-branch name is still validated, so Commit Changes is refused with 'New branch name must be a well-formed Git reference name.' even though no new branch will be created.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared form still binds/validates NewBranchName from the inactive branch field; switching CommitChoice back does not clear or disable that field, so its GitRefName validation still rejects the form.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s file editor (also Delete and Upload), after typing an invalid name under 'Create a new branch for this commit' and then switching to 'Commit directly to the branch', the hidden new-branch name is still validated, so Commit Changes is refused with 'New branch name must be a well-formed Git reference name.' even though no new branch will be created.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on Upload File, two files with the same name can be added to the same upload. Both are listed as uploaded and Commit Changes succeeds without any warning, but only one of them is committed; the other's content is silently discarded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UploadRepoFiles stages each upload using its original name as the index path without rejecting duplicate target paths, so the final blob wins.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on Upload File, two files with the same name can be added to the same upload. Both are listed as uploaded and Commit Changes succeeds without any warning, but only one of them is committed; the other's content is silently discarded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a fork branch that has its own commits but nothing new upstream (the upstream branch was created later at the common base), the banner wrongly says upstream has new changes, and confirming Sync fork shows "server error: 500".
logicalBugs.rootCause: GetBranchDivergingInfo uses branch UpdatedUnix timestamps when its fast path cannot calculate divergence, so a newly created upstream branch at an older common commit is incorrectly marked as having new commits. MergeUpstream then attempts a merge instead of returning up-to-date.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a fork branch that has its own commits but nothing new upstream (the upstream branch was created later at the common base), the banner wrongly says upstream has new changes, and confirming Sync fork shows "server error: 500".

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a source-file URL can select a range of lines using a fragment such as #L1-L3. Opening a range that starts at nonexistent line zero, such as #L0-L3, displays a JavaScript error banner instead of safely ignoring or handling the invalid line number.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Line selection uses one-based line indexes from the hash without rejecting zero before indexing line DOM elements.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a source-file URL can select a range of lines using a fragment such as #L1-L3. Opening a range that starts at nonexistent line zero, such as #L0-L3, displays a JavaScript error banner instead of safely ignoring or handling the invalid line number.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when Apply Patch rejects an invalid new-branch name (for example one with consecutive dots), the page reloads with the patch and the error, but the Propose file change / Commit Changes button stays disabled after the name is corrected. Only editing the patch text itself re-enables it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: After the validation response, editor dirty tracking treats the restored patch as its clean baseline and watches only fields outside .commit-form-wrapper. Branch and message corrections are excluded, so only changing patch text enables commit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when Apply Patch rejects an invalid new-branch name (for example one with consecutive dots), the page reloads with the patch and the error, but the Propose file change / Commit Changes button stays disabled after the name is corrected. Only editing the patch text itself re-enables it.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, open a commit diff limited with ?files=<path>. Only that file’s diff is shown, but the changed-files tree still lists all files without a filter indicator; clicking an excluded file does nothing because its diff anchor is absent.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The diff file tree uses the commit full changed-file summary while only the body is filtered; it renders links to absent body anchors without a filter indicator or navigation behavior.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, open a commit diff limited with ?files=<path>. Only that file’s diff is shown, but the changed-files tree still lists all files without a filter indicator; clicking an excluded file does nothing because its diff anchor is absent.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, searching a repository’s Branches list limits the rows to matching branch names. Deleting or restoring a branch from those results succeeds but clears the search and returns to the unfiltered list. The current page number can remain, so a result on page 2 can lead to unrelated branches on unfiltered page 2. The failure concerns losing the active search after the action, not a failed deletion or restoration.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared redirect used after branch deletion and restoration constructs the Branches address with only the page parameter. The action buttons also pass the page but omit the search query, so the server cannot preserve the active search when redirecting.
reproductionPaths: Open a repository’s Branches page and search for a prefix shared by several branch names. Delete a matching branch and confirm, or restore a deleted matching branch. The action succeeds, but the resulting page has an empty search box and shows branches outside the searched prefix; when started on a later results page, that page number is retained without its search.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a file’s History lists the commits that changed its old path, including the commit that renamed or deleted it. The View at this point in history link on that removal commit still opens the old path in that commit and returns 404, because the path no longer exists there. Links to earlier versions and the removal commit’s View changes link can work correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The history query includes commits that remove the requested path. The history template nevertheless builds every snapshot link from that row’s commit ID and the unchanged history path, without resolving a renamed destination or suppressing the link when the old path is absent from the selected commit.
reproductionPaths: Create a file, commit it, edit and commit it again, then rename or delete it in another commit. Open History for the original file path and choose View at this point in history on the rename or deletion commit. The snapshot opens a 404 saying the old path does not exist; snapshots from the earlier commits and View changes for the removal commit remain usable.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a fork is a copy of another repository that may have a different name. When comparing a differently named fork’s branch against its upstream repository, View File links in the comparison combine the fork’s owner with the upstream repository’s name. They open the wrong repository address and can show 404 instead of the compared file. The comparison itself can display the changes correctly, and comparisons inside the fork or forks retaining the upstream name hide the error.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The comparison handler passes the head fork’s owner but the base repository’s name into the shared source-path builder. That mismatched owner/name pair is then used for both the changed-file source links and the before-change source links, instead of using the head fork’s own repository name.
reproductionPaths: Fork a repository under a different name, add a file on a branch in the fork, and compare that branch against upstream. Open the changed file’s menu and click View File. Its address uses the fork owner with the upstream repository name and returns 404 when that repository does not exist. Two-dot and three-dot comparisons are affected, including links for deleted files.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, clicking a matched line number in repository code search navigates to the file, but Markdown opens as formatted text instead of numbered source. The address contains a line fragment such as #L9, yet that rendered view has no corresponding target, so the matched line is neither selected nor scrolled into view. This is a missing line target after successful navigation; an allegation that clicking does not navigate is a different claim.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Search-result line links include a commit, file path and line fragment but omit the display=source option. The file viewer renders Markdown by default, and that rendered output lacks the source view’s numbered line targets. Existing source-line permalinks supply the missing option, but code-search links do not.
reproductionPaths: Search a repository’s code for text present in a Markdown file and click the number beside a matching line. The file opens at a commit-specific address ending in #L followed by the line number, but the page displays formatted Markdown with no numbered or highlighted target line. Switching to View Source reveals the numbered text; equivalent links to ordinary text files work.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s source-file view, a text file ending with a newline has a header line count one greater than the last numbered line displayed. For example, two lines each terminated by a newline produce a 3 lines header but only lines 1 and 2 in the body. Files without a final newline have matching counts. No explanatory trailing-newline marker makes the extra count clear; the report need not claim any saved content is missing.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The file header counts newline characters plus one, intentionally counting the empty line after a final newline. The source renderer omits that final empty line, and the page does not implement the suggested explanatory marker, so two different counting conventions appear together without explanation.
reproductionPaths: Create a text file containing first line, a newline, second line and a final newline, then open its source view. Compare the 3 lines header with numbered lines ending at 2. Remove the final newline as a control and the header and displayed numbering agree.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, the complete filename .. can be entered in Add File > New File. Committing it is refused, but the banner’s expandable Error Message exposes raw Git failure output and the server’s temporary repository path instead of the usual invalid-filename message. This accepted path requires the filename .. through the rendered editor; a handcrafted ../escape.txt request is outside it, and ordinary UI entry of ../escape.txt is normalized. No successful traversal or access outside the repository is established.
logicalBugs.rootCause: File validation checks a cleaned version of the requested path, but the later Git index lookup receives the original path. The complete name .. therefore reaches git ls-files, which rejects it as outside the repository. The resulting wrapped Git error, including its temporary working-directory path, is rendered through the generic file-update failure message instead of being classified as invalid input.
reproductionPaths: Open a repository branch and choose Add File > New File. Enter exactly .. as the complete filename, supply content and submit Commit Changes. Expand Error Message in the failure banner: it contains a Git ls-files error and a temporary server repository path. The commit is refused and the form remains; this is not a full-page crash or evidence of successful path traversal.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea repository code search without a code indexer, an initial search that supplies no search mode can show Exact selected while actually running case-insensitive Words matching. Clicking Search again without changing the displayed query or mode then explicitly selects Exact and can change the results. This matches disagreement between the displayed mode and the first search’s effective mode; Exact mode’s normal case-sensitive behavior is not itself the failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Git-based search backend defaults an absent search mode to Words, while the search-type selector defaults its displayed value to the first supported mode, Exact. Because the absent-mode request and the unchanged resubmitted form use different effective modes, identical-looking searches yield different results.
reproductionPaths: With the repository code indexer disabled, use the repository home’s Search code box to search for a lowercase word that appears only with an initial capital in a file. The results page shows Exact selected but still finds the capitalized text. Click Search again without changing anything: the address now includes search_mode=exact and that result disappears. A direct code-search address containing only the query reproduces the same initial mismatch.
